observations.note: Native 1x transparent view delivered by pixl_inspection as an unmodified 16x16 PNG block (sha256 515a100d...). One light sky-blue check mark on transparent ground: a short left arm rising from the vertex to the left and a much longer right arm rising to the upper right. No plate, box, halo or fringe. Host did not report any resizing of the block.

Native 1x on #172336 (the consumer display.background). The blue mark separates cleanly from the navy panel; the check shape and the short-left/long-right asymmetry are legible at native size. No detail merges into the panel colour.

3x nearest on #172336 (the consumer display.scale/filter). Chunky diagonal strokes made of consistent 1-pixel-per-row stair clusters, pointed single-pixel tips at both arm ends, one single-pixel vertex at the bottom. Left arm spans 3 columns and rises 4 rows; right arm spans 7 columns and rises 8 rows. No stray pixels, blur or soft edges.
Native 1x on checkerboard. Confirms a transparent background: the checker shows through everywhere except the 29 mark pixels; no translucent matte or halo visible around the mark.
3x nearest on checkerboard. Same single-colour hard-edged check mark; edges are crisp against both checker tones, confirming binary alpha without fringe pixels.

verdicts.reason: Measured: PNG IHDR 16x16, 8-bit RGBA, single frame (frame_count 1, n_frames 1), no horizontal strip or extra canvas (pixl_asset_check width/height 16 pass; pixel-dump size [16,16]).

Measured: alpha histogram {0: 227, 255: 29}; every pixel outside the single 29-pixel mark component has alpha 0; all four edge rows/columns fully transparent; no matte, box or fringe (fractional_alpha_pixels 0, opaque_components 1). Checkerboard views 3 and 4 confirm visually.

Viewed in views 1 and 2 on #172336 (and 0, 3, 4): the image is a check mark whose left arm (3 columns wide, 4 rows tall, 7 pixels) is clearly shorter and shallower than the right arm (7 columns, 8 rows, 19 pixels); the mark is visibly not mirror-symmetric about its vertex at column 6 (exact mirror test false). The tick form conveys successful completion.

Viewed alone (view 1 at 1x and view 2 at 3x on the panel colour), the single tick reads as done/success. It is not a spinner, dots or loop (activity), not an X or warning (failure), not paired bars (pause), and not the rightward play triangle of assets/start.svg (idle Start).

View 1 (16x16 on #172336) and view 2 (48x48 nearest on #172336) both show a readable check silhouette; the short-left/long-right asymmetry remains visible at 1x and is unmistakable at 3x. Nothing is lost into the panel colour (mark luma 169 vs panel luma 34).

The mark's only visible colour is sky blue rgba(112,185,237,255) = #70b9ed, the same cool blue as the assets/start.svg fill; viewed on the navy panel it reads as the existing UI accent. Judged as a visual relationship; the exact-hex equality is an observation, not the rule applied.

In the derived desaturated views (work/queue.ready/rev3/inspection/derived-desaturated-1x-on-172336.png 16x16 and derived-desaturated-3x-on-172336.png 48x48, luma composite on #172336) the mark remains a distinct, identifiable check shape at both 1x and 3x; its meaning is carried by form. Packet views 0-4 were all observed; the grayscale derivatives are supplementary derived evidence, not candidates.

Views 2 and 4 at 3x show deliberate construction: one flat colour, hard binary edges, consistent 1px-per-row diagonal stair clusters, pointed tips, one connected component, no stray pixels, blur, anti-aliasing or downscaled-illustration artifacts. The flat single-accent chunky-stroke treatment could plausibly be extended to Working, Retry and Paused; this does not approve the family style.
